# Speech fixtures

`swedish.wav` is a canonical 16 kHz mono PCM16 copy of the CC BY 4.0 FLEURS recording `fleurs-529121125980696453.wav` (7.8 seconds).
`long.wav` concatenates all three Swedish FLEURS recordings in `fleurs.json` order (38.7 seconds, two male clips and one female clip). `silence.wav` is two seconds of generated silence.

`fleurs-*.wav`: three recordings from Google FLEURS, Swedish (`sv_se`), test split, rows 0, 3 and 6.
Source: https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/fleurs
Archive: https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/fleurs/resolve/main/data/sv_se/audio/test.tar.gz
Reference text: https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/fleurs/resolve/main/data/sv_se/test.tsv
Attribution: Google, FLEURS: Few-shot Learning Evaluation of Universal Representations of Speech.
License: CC BY 4.0, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/
Modification: converted the original float WAV to 16 kHz mono PCM16 using FFmpeg.
Original filenames and transcriptions are preserved in `fleurs.json`.

`reference-int8.json` and `reference-int4.json` are generated by `scripts/reference.py` using
onnx-asr 0.12.0 and ONNX Runtime 1.30.0 CPU, from the pinned unmodified Klang model files, explicitly including the published `nemo128.onnx` preprocessor.
They are reference-engine outputs, not claims of perfect recognition against the human transcript.
The three natural speech samples are a compatibility smoke test, not a representative WER benchmark.

`formats/` contains CC BY 4.0 derivatives of `swedish.wav`. FFmpeg produced 44.1 kHz stereo PCM WAV/MP3/Vorbis and 48 kHz stereo AAC/Opus/FLAC. `long.*` contains two cycles of `long.wav` (77.4 seconds); `delayed.m4a` has a five-second container start offset. These check downmixing, resampling, codec priming, window continuity and audio-relative timestamps. MP3 uses libmp3lame at 128 kbit/s, AAC uses 128 kbit/s, and other codecs use FFmpeg defaults. Vorbis was generated with `-c:a vorbis -strict -2`.

Run `python3 scripts/fixtures.py` with FFmpeg installed to regenerate the Swedish WAV and codec derivatives. The generated files preserve the FLEURS attribution and license above.

Long endurance files are generated into ignored temporary/test output paths, not versioned. The >2-hour WAV contains five copies of the FLEURS utterance at 0, 28, 1798, 3598 and 7198 seconds, with silence between them. It checks elapsed-time boundaries, not continuous two-hour conversation accuracy. The decoder-only WAV uses a deterministic PCM ramp throughout; no model is used for that check.

To reproduce the optional >2-hour MP3 decoding check:

```
ffmpeg -v error -y -stream_loop 102 -i tests/fixtures/formats/long.mp3 -t 7210 -c:a copy /tmp/pianissimo-two-hour.mp3
LARGE_MP3=/tmp/pianissimo-two-hour.mp3 npx playwright test tests/file-audio.spec.ts
```

`multilingual/` contains one human-recorded Google FLEURS test sample each for English (`en_us`), German (`de_de`), French (`fr_fr`), Danish (`da_dk`), and Russian (`ru_ru`). Dataset revision, original filenames, human transcriptions and language configurations are recorded in `multilingual/fleurs.json`. Samples were taken from `data/<config>/audio/test.tar.gz`, with reference text from `data/<config>/test.tsv`, at that pinned dataset revision. Attribution: Google FLEURS, CC BY 4.0 (same source/license as above). Audio was converted to 16 kHz mono PCM16 with FFmpeg. `long-en.wav` repeats the English sample five times to cross a 30-second inference boundary.

`multilingual/reference-parakeet.json` is generated by `scripts/reference-parakeet.py` with onnx-asr 0.12.0, ONNX Runtime 1.30.0, and Parakeet's exact pinned `nemo128.onnx` preprocessor. Native and WASM predictions can differ; regression checks compare both transcripts against the human reference, requiring no more word errors in the browser. This is a five-clip smoke test, not validation of all 25 languages or a representative accuracy benchmark.
